title: Unexpected Overnight Smart Plug Load
dataSources: Zigbee2MQTT device reports (`zigbee2mqtt:device`), Shelly/Tasmota telemetry (`shelly:status`, `tasmota:sensor`), Hue bridge events (`hue:event`), Nest/Ecobee thermostat (`ecobee:thermostat`), door/leak/motion sensors.
app: Philips Hue, smart plugs (Tasmota/Shelly/TP-Link Kasa), thermostats (Nest/Ecobee), locks, and Zigbee/Z-Wave sensors via MQTT / Zigbee2MQTT and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=shelly:status
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour>=0 AND hour<5
| stats avg(power_w) as avg_power by device
| where avg_power>50
| sort - avg_power
description: Flags plugs that are drawing meaningful power while the house should be asleep, catching the forgotten heater, game console, or dehumidifier left running overnight.
value: Nighttime baseload is where sneaky energy waste hides; this query turns it into a simple ranked list you can actually act on.
implementation: Send Shelly power telemetry to Splunk; review overnight averages weekly and inspect the surprise devices at the top.
visualization: Leaderboard of overnight average power by smart plug.
grandmaExplanation: It counts which plugged-in things are quietly burning power in the middle of the night when they probably should not be.
